poster_title: Seeing, Listening, Remembering, and Reasoning: A Multimodal Agent with Long-Term Memory
authors: Lin Long, Yichen He, Wentao Ye, Yiyuan Pan, Yuan Lin, Hang Li, Junbo Zhao, Wei Li

content: Multimodal agents require real-time processing of visual and auditory inputs.
Traditional methods focus on low-level details, lacking long-term context.
LVQA benchmarks need to evaluate higher-level cognitive abilities.
Handle infinite multimodal input streams in real-time.
Incrementally build and maintain consistent world knowledge.
M3-Agent processes real-time inputs to construct episodic and semantic memories.
Episodic memory captures concrete events; semantic memory stores general knowledge.
Entity-centric memory structure enables coherent reasoning over time.
Reinforcement learning for multi-turn reasoning and iterative memory retrieval.
panels.figure_caption: DAPO training process: average scores (training set) and accuracy (dev set) curves

content: Evaluated on M3-Bench: 100 robot-perspective videos, 920 web-sourced videos.
M3-Bench includes five question types for memory-based reasoning.
M3-Agent outperforms Gemini-GPT4o-Hybrid by 6.7%, 7.7%, and 5.3% on M3-Bench-robot, M3-Bench-web, and VideoMME-long.
Ablation studies highlight the importance of semantic memory and reinforcement learning.
M3-Agent demonstrates superior performance in long-term memory and reasoning tasks.
M3-Agent advances multimodal agents toward human-like long-term memory and reasoning.
Provides insights for designing practical multimodal agents with long-term memory.

Fig7.caption: Figure 4 Average scores (on training set) and accuracy (on dev set) curves during the DAPO training process.
